funder_name: Center for Language Education and Cooperation (CLEC), China
funding_summary: As described in the Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU) guide for its master's programme: full tuition, accommodation, a living allowance of RMB 3,000 a month, and comprehensive medical insurance (RMB 800 per person per academic year). Tuition and accommodation amounts are not specified.
summary: Scholarship for students and currently employed Chinese-language teachers recommended by approved institutions such as Confucius Institutes and Chinese embassies or consulates abroad. This entry records the 2026 SYSU guide for the Master's in Teaching Chinese to Speakers of Other Languages (MTCSOL), up to two academic years from September 2026. Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens aged 18 to 35 on 1 September 2026 (currently employed teachers up to 45), hold a bachelor's degree, and have HSK Level 5 with at least 210 points and HSKK Intermediate with at least 60 points. Two academic recommendation letters and a letter from the recommending institution are required. Applicants register on the CLEC platform (chinese.cn) and on the SYSU system, upload a study plan of over 3,000 words, and final admission depends on CLEC expert review. Other universities publish their own versions with different programmes and requirements. The official CLEC site could not be opened when this was researched.
source_publisher: Sun Yat-sen University, International Student Office
route_name: Register on the CLEC platform and apply to the host university (SYSU system)
deadline_source_text: 15 May 2026 (Beijing Time) at SYSU for the September 2026 intake. No time of day stated. Other universities set their own deadlines.

programme_title: Chinese Government Scholarship - Bilateral Program (Type A)
funding_summary: Tuition, accommodation, living expenses and comprehensive medical insurance. The SYSU page gives no amounts; funding standards follow the China Scholarship Council's annual announcement.
teaching_language: Chinese or English (depends on the programme)
summary: Type A scholarship applied for through a candidate's home-country channel, usually the Chinese embassy or consulate, and the CSC portal at campuschina.org. This entry records the 2026 SYSU guide: non-Chinese citizens with a valid foreign passport, generally no older than 25 for bachelor's, 35 for master's and 40 for doctoral studies; only majors on SYSU's approved 2026 list are valid. Bachelor's applicants take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA). Proof of language is HSK for Chinese-taught programmes or TOEFL iBT 79 / IELTS 6.5 for English-taught ones. Study plans are about 3,000 words for master's and 6,000 for doctoral applicants. Applicants apply to both the CSC system and the SYSU system; final admission depends on CSC expert review. Other universities publish their own guides.
source_publisher: Sun Yat-sen University, International Student Office
route_name: Home-country recommendation, CSC portal (Type A) and the university system
deadline_source_text: The CSC accepts recommendations on a rolling basis and the SYSU page gives no final date; confirm with the home-country dispatching authority or the Chinese embassy. SYSU invitation-letter pre-application deadlines were 12 January and 12 February 2026.

programme_title: Tsinghua University - Graduate Admissions and Scholarships for International Students (CGS and BGS)
funding_summary: The admissions page names two scholarships. Chinese Government Scholarship: full awards usually cover tuition, housing or a housing subsidy, a stipend and medical insurance; partial awards cover some of these. Beijing Government Scholarship: usually tuition and medical insurance for one academic year. No Tsinghua-specific scholarships are described on the page.
teaching_language: Chinese or English (set by each programme)
summary: Admissions information for foreign nationals applying to Tsinghua master's and doctoral programmes for 2027 entry. Applicants must not hold Chinese nationality and must have a valid foreign passport; master's applicants need a bachelor's degree and doctoral applicants a master's degree (some schools admit bachelor's holders directly to doctoral study). Overseas degrees must be authenticated by CSCSE before registration. Language requirements and any work-experience conditions are set by each programme. Applications generally run from September to February, with deadlines set by each school or department, and an RMB 800 non-refundable application fee is paid online. Scholarships are awarded after admission through the Chinese Government Scholarship and Beijing Government Scholarship routes.
deadline_source_text: Generally September to February, but each school, department and programme sets its own deadline in its catalogue. The winter break runs 21 January to 17 February 2027, so verification may be delayed.
